conviction_note: The quarter is pre-guided: Q4 adj EPS $1.25-1.35, consensus $1.30-1.31, whisper $1.35. The move turns on the first FY27 guide. Street FY27 is $3.34, about flat on a FY26 base that carries a ~$64m IEEPA tariff-refund COGS benefit. Last November the first guide came in 7% under the street and the stock fell 18.5%. Into this print the stock is up ~25% since the August report and sits above the $22 mean target. That gives a mild negative lean (p_up 44) on a ~10% abs move. The finding sum (-2.0) and the scaled number (-1.2) differ only because p_up carries the guide's two-sided uncertainty, and a ~10%-of-shares short (7.6 days to cover) argues against sizing the negative larger.

next_guide.basis: This is the first FY27 guide. The street has FY27 about flat on FY26 ($3.31), but FY26 adj results include a $64.1m nine-month IEEPA refund COGS benefit (10-Q). Last year's first guide came in 7% under the street. The FY27 tailwinds are the end of Project Momentum cash costs, the APS brand transition (~$30m) and the absence of IEEPA tariffs. A guide below $3.34 at the midpoint is somewhat more likely than one above it, but this is not established.

findings.finding: The first FY27 guide lands against a street FY27 adj EPS of $3.34 ($3.30-3.39, 3 analysts), essentially flat on FY26's ~$3.31. FY26 adj results include a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit of $64.1m in COGS over nine months (~$0.70/share pre-offsets; part of it reverses tariffs paid in FY26 itself). Matching the street therefore needs real underlying growth in a battery category that management said worsened through Q3. Last year's first guide (FY26 $3.30-3.60, midpoint $3.45) was 7% under the $3.72 FactSet consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-18: FY26 initial guide below street plus a Q1 guide of $0.20-0.30 -> -18.49% (baseline; https://finviz.com/news/376900/energizer-shares-fall-after-earnings-miss-and-cautious-outlook). 2026-08-04: back-half organic cut -> +2.18% (the cut was already expected).
findings.source_date: 2026-11-16 (page read; consensus with no revisions in 4 weeks)
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus of $3.34 implies the street expects the company to replace a one-off refund with operating growth. If the market doubted that, the stock would not be 9% above the $22 mean target after a 25% run. The refund detail sits in the 10-Q's COGS note, not in the wire previews, which focus on the Q4 margin.
findings.independence: 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001632790/000163279026000076/enr-20260630.htm) for the $64.1m COGS benefit; the Nov-2025 guide history from finviz (https://finviz.com/news/376900/energizer-shares-fall-after-earnings-miss-and-cautious-outlook). The tailwinds (Momentum costs ending, ~$30m APS brand transition, no IEEPA tariffs going forward, https://finviz.com/news/420384/energizers-clean-40-gross-margin-faces-its-test-as-battery-demand-softens) cut the other way, which is why the range is wide.

findings.finding: Expectations are elevated going in. ENR rose ~25% from the 2026-08-04 report to $25.06 on 2026-11-10, against a slipping S&P and a staples ETF up ~8% in a month. Spot $24.04 is 9% above the $22 mean target (Hold consensus; UBS $22 on 11-11, Canaccord cut to $17 on 10-23). The whisper is $1.35, the top of the Q4 guide. A print merely inside the guide meets a bar set above consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 5 of 7 prior prints fell (baseline). The last time the stock ran into a print on margin optimism (Aug 2025, +26.7%) it paid off, but that print carried a $78.5m retroactive production credit.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself the pricing. The question is whether the release clears the higher whisper and guide bar. Had the market been cautious, spot would sit near targets and short interest would be rising, not falling.
findings.independence: Targets from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/enr/forecast/ (different source). XLP context from https://www.foxbusiness.com/quote?stockTicker=XLP.

findings.finding: Q4 is pre-guided at adj EPS $1.25-1.35 with a 'clean' gross margin above 40% (no tariff credits), pricing neutral after Q3's promotions and Project Momentum savings. Consensus of $1.30-1.31 sits at the guide midpoint. Energizer has hit or beaten EPS in 2 of the last 4 quarters (Q1 and Q2 FY26 beat; Q3 FY26 and Q4 FY25 missed), so a print at or near the top of the range is plausible but the line is guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 EPS miss -> +2.18%; Q4 FY25 miss -> -18.49% (moved by the guide); Q1 FY26 beat ($0.31 vs $0.26) -> -0.09%. The stock has not paid for in-guide quarterly beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the result lands inside a company guide and the whisper sits at its top. Kept small.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/420384/energizers-clean-40-gross-margin-faces-its-test-as-battery-demand-softens) gives the same bar, $1.31.

findings.finding: Q4 sales line: the company guided organic flat to down LSD after saying the battery category softened 200-300bp versus expectations and worsened through Q3. The May scanner reading showed the category -3.4% over 4 weeks. Revenue consensus is $813.3m (-2.3% y/y on $832.8m). No independent Jul-Sep category series was found, so the trend after the call is unknown, and continued worsening would also weigh on the FY27 organic guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-04 back-half organic cut from ~4% to flat/+1% -> +2.18%. The stock looked through the sales cut that time.
findings.why_not_priced: The cut is public. What is not visible is whether the category kept deteriorating in Jul-Sep; the preview flags lean retailer inventories as a replenishment risk.
findings.independence: The preview (https://finviz.com/news/420384/energizers-clean-40-gross-margin-faces-its-test-as-battery-demand-softens) restates the 200-300bp softening and inventory risk. Shares the company's own call as its root source.

findings.finding: Largest-channel counterparty: Walmart's Q2 FY27 (May-Jul 2026, overlapping ENR's Q4 by one month) showed US comp ex-fuel slowing to +2.6% from +4.6%, general merchandise up only LSD, a softer consumer, and price rollbacks planned for the back half. That points to promotional pressure and cautious replenishment in mass channels during ENR's Q4 and Q1.
findings.link: Walmart is a major US mass retailer for batteries and auto care; ENR's 10-Q says North America sales go through large retailers but does not name them or give a percentage here, so no figure is stated. The quarters overlap by one month (July).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history; ENR's Q3 promotional spending was cited for its margin miss (Aug 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy dated three months ago and widely read; included for breadth and sized small.
findings.independence: Walmart corporate release https://corporate.walmart.com/news/2026/08/20/walmart-releases-q2-fy27-earnings. It is a proxy for ENR, not confirmed by ENR.

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Edgewell (EPC) reported its Sep-quarter on 2026-11-12 with organic +3.1% (North America +3.3%) and adjusted gross margin 45.7% (+510bp). Its first FY27 guide was adj EPS $1.85-2.15 (midpoint +3.6% on $1.93) with organic +1-3%. A US personal-care peer in the same mass channel guided modest growth, not a cut.
findings.link: Edgewell was spun from the same Energizer parent in 2015 and sells through the same US mass/drug/club channel; it has no battery or auto-care exposure, so it shares the channel only, not the category.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since 11-12 and partly in ENR's price path. It tells you little about batteries, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Quiet 2026 hurricane season: CSU's August update cut the US major-landfall probability to 16% (historical average 43%) with El Nino strengthening. Only tropical storms (Arthur in June, Bertha in July) made US landfall by the reports found. That leaves little storm-driven battery demand in ENR's Jul-Sep quarter.
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (CSU August update as reported; year confirmed by the El Nino/2026 season references in the article)
findings.why_not_priced: Weather-to-company transmission is not confirmed by ENR. It was largely knowable when ENR set its Q4 guide on 08-04, so it is mostly inside the guide.

findings.why_not_priced: Short positioning is asymmetric: it is not a directional view, but it makes an upside surprise move more than a downside one of the same size.

findings.finding: $53m of the ~$64m IEEPA refund receivable was still uncollected after the Q3 call ($11m received after June quarter-end). Management expects it through FY26 and into FY27, but CBP's CAPE Phase 3 missed its 2026-08-20 target and finally-liquidated entries are contested. The cash update in the release can go either way for FCF and deleveraging.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (receivable booked, $48m in P&L) -> -7.70% on 2026-05-05 per baseline; the refund did not lift the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is below operating income and a cash-timing item. Sized at a fraction because no path to the guide is stated beyond FCF.
findings.independence: Keyt/Stacker 2026-09-22 on stuck refunds (https://keyt.com/stacker-international/2026/09/22/months-after-ieepa-tariffs-were-struck-down-some-refunds-remain-caught-between-customs-and-the-courts/); shares the 10-Q with finding 1 (different line: cash vs EPS base).

baseline_tension: The skew is unavailable (null), and the call-heavy OI plus a 25% run-up say the market leans long into the print. The mild negative here cuts against that lean, and the falling-but-elevated short interest cuts against the negative. That is why p_up sits at 44 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): ~11-12% of float short at 7.6 days to cover, so the next-guide negative went from -1.5 to -1.3 and the expectations negative from -1.5 to -1.2.
Pessimism artefact / own caveat (lesson 3): with no skew and a call-heavy book, p_up moved from 42 to 44, so the scaled number went from -1.6 to -1.2.
Lessons 2 and 5 left the sizes standing: the refund receivable is already sized as a small one_off, and the hurricane and Walmart proxies were already small.
Lesson 6: the bar is sourced to a company guide plus two agreeing estimates, so no cap was applied.
